extracted.intended_audience: literate London readers (gentlemen and women) interested in manners, letter-writing, and social conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Short social-advice essays on personal conduct: how to raise and educate children for worldly success, how to behave and be flattered in company, and how to write letters of gallantry so they succeed. Advice is practical and illustrated with examples and anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter-writing: be as near what you speak face to face as you can
rubrics_metrics.description: There was no rule in the world to be made for writing letters, but that of being as near what you speak face to face as you can.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write letters to a mistress as if speaking to her in person; avoid excessive plaintiveness or complaint (which 'has lost more mistresses than any one mistake'). Prefer pleasant, diverting tone over languishing sorrow. Examples: John Careless's negligent, lively letter versus Colonel Constant's solemn, plaintive epistle — the pleasant, gay letter often wins where the mournful one gains only pity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor education to children's temper and inclinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Be particularly observant of the temper and inclinations of childhood and youth, that we may not give vice and folly supplies from the growing generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match schooling and future stations to each child's disposition: a plodding, provident child may be trained for commerce/citizenship; an arrogant or witty youth may be sent to university to be exposed to raillery that teaches humility; a subtle, restrained child may be placed as a page to a lady to learn manners and social arts. The purpose is to place children where their natural tendencies are best cultivated for family advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good breeding outweighs learning in social success
rubrics_metrics.description: Wisdom, valour, justice, and learning can't keep a man in countenance if he wants that less art of life and behaviour, called 'good breeding.' Good breeding is an expedient to make fools and wise men equals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a graceful manner, familiarity with conversation, and courtly mien: 'living in conversation from infancy' prepares one to meet witty and wise people without embarrassment. Ceremony and good manners are practical tools that often carry a man further in court and society than mere learning or intellect (examples: Will. Courtly and other social exemplars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flattery for 'Platonics': subtle consent rather than panegyric
rubrics_metrics.description: A Platonne is not to be touched with panegyric: you are not therefore to commend, but silently consent to all she does, and says. Consider that in her the scorn of you is not humour, but opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dealing with philosophically inclined or 'platonic' women, avoid gross or direct flattery; instead show tacit agreement and deferential admiration. Treat scorn as ideological distance to be handled by subtlety. Illustration: anecdote of a rake and an attempted Protestant nunnery shows how gross approaches fail, while measured, sly behaviour disarms such women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spoken wit often fails when printed
rubrics_metrics.description: How small an appearance the prettiest things said in company, make when in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume that lively repartee or the finest points of conversation will have the same effect once transcribed. Be cautious about printing conversational anecdotes or 'bright conversation' expecting equal effect on readers; the context and delivery in person matter greatly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public dress must observe decorum
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice to all persons that dress themselves as they please, without regard to decorum (as with blue and red stockings in mourning; tucked cravats, and nightcap wigs, before people of the first quality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain appropriate attire according to social situations (no inappropriate colored stockings in mourning, no tucked cravats or informal wigs in the presence of the highest quality). Those who flout decorum are expected to comply with social demands or leave; rumors of payoffs to tolerate such 'enormities' are 'utterly false and scandalous.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial assessment of tutors and pupils by merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Bickerstaff has taken the two famous universities of this land under his immediate care... and to correct them impartially, by placing them in orders and classes in the learned world, according to their merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adjudicating scholarly or pedagogical standing, hear both sides and rank tutors and pupils impartially on merit rather than reputation or faction. Promise to receive intelligence and classify accordingly (procedural commitment rather than detailed scoring rules).
